Di-8-ANEPPS controls of Semenov et al. (2025), on DANDI:001272¶

Paper: Semenov, Kim, Silkuniene & Pakhomov (2025), "Excitation and polarization of isolated neurons by high-frequency sine waves for temporal interference stimulation", Cell Reports Physical Science 6, 102660, doi:10.1016/j.xcrp.2025.102660.

Dataset: DANDI:001272, "The Use of Di8-ANEPPS to Evaluate Neuronal Sensitivity to Unmodulated Sine Waves", version 0.250805.1358. The paper cites the dandiset without a version. Two versions are published, 0.250701.1622 and 0.250805.1358; both hold the same 65 files with the same blobs (checked below), so the most recent published version is pinned.

Claims: claims/001272/10.1016-j.xcrp.2025.102660.yaml, written from the NIH author manuscript (PMC12320893) with its STAR Methods and supplement. Its header items F1 to F6 and O1 to O6 are cited below by label; the helper sinewave.py says where every parameter comes from.

The FluoVolt reference group of the two with_inputs claims comes from the paper's other deposits, DANDI:001032 (0.240527.1432), 001033 (0.240527.1432) and 001035 (0.240527.1432): their 250-ms unmodulated 2-kHz sessions in NaCl solution. DANDI:001034 (0.240527.1431) is loaded only to compare its 2-kHz unmodulated files with those of 001032; DANDI:001271 (0.250805.1352) is used for one unit check. The claims on the other deposits are tested in fluovolt_elsewhere.ipynb.

Data check¶

What was loaded, and each check of the metadata against the values. The stimulus of each session is known only from its session_description (frequency, amplitude in volts, and the files' conversion "1V translates to 36 V/cm at the location of neurons"). The onset is not stored; F3 puts it 50 ms into the session.

The ROI readings are therefore O1 (a), O1 (b) (identical to (a) wherever erosion empties it) and the whole deposited 16 x 16 frame. The deposited frames are a crop around the soma (the Methods image 64 x 64 pixels), so the whole frame is the closest available reading of "the emission over the entire cell soma"; it is run beside the claims file's two readings.

Clock check¶

The files carry no stimulus timing, so the onset at 50 ms (F3) is checked against the responses: the jump of the inverted dF over the 20 ms after a candidate onset, against the 20 ms before it, in every session, at the true onset and at shifted ones. If the onset is right, the contrast peaks at 50 ms.

In [5]:
def onset_contrast(recs, onset_ms, invert=True, roi="whole"):
    vals = []
    for r in recs:
        y = sw.dff(r["traces"][roi], r["t"], "a", invert=invert)
        t = r["t"]
        vals.append(y[(t >= onset_ms) & (t < onset_ms + 20)].mean() - y[(t >= onset_ms - 20) & (t < onset_ms)].mean())
    return np.array(vals)

shifts = [25, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 100, 150, 200, 250, 320]
cc = pd.DataFrame({f"{s} ms": [onset_contrast(D, s).mean()] for s in shifts}, index=["mean contrast (% dF)"])
print(cc.round(3).to_string())
c50 = onset_contrast(D, 50)
print(f"at 50 ms the contrast is positive in {np.sum(c50 > 0)} of {len(c50)} sessions")

Session tables under every reading¶

For each combination of O1 (ROI), O2 (F0) and O3 (AP height), each session's APs are detected on the inverted trace (F1) and, for figs1-aps-as-emission-decrease, on the trace as recorded. Reading names are roi/f0/height.

O3 takes an AP's width at half height between 1 and 20 ms. The claims file had 2 to 20 ms when this attempt was first run; a reader amended it after the question in questions/001272.yaml, as the Methods' "lasted about 10 ms" is the whole AP duration. Every claim below is tested with the 1-ms bound, and the result with the earlier 2-ms bound is printed beside it to show what the change did.

The AP height is read two ways. As the dF value at the peak (the Methods' "APs peaked at a more than 5% dF"), the claims file's reading, run first; and as the peak's prominence, a variant added after verification round 1, since on the inverted Di-8-ANEPPS trace bleaching raises the baseline and noise peaks on a raised baseline then pass a height measured as the value. A null test shows how many detections each reading makes where no AP is expected: in the frames before the onset and in those from 10 ms after the stimulus to the end of the recording.

In [6]:
def rname(k):
    return "/".join(k)

TABW = {w: {k: sw.session_table(D, *k, invert=True, min_width_ms=w) for k in sw.READINGS} for w in (1.0, 2.0)}
RAWW = {w: {k: sw.session_table(D, *k, invert=False, min_width_ms=w) for k in sw.READINGS} for w in (1.0, 2.0)}
THW = {w: {k: sw.thresholds(TABW[w][k]) for k in sw.READINGS} for w in (1.0, 2.0)}
TABP = {k: sw.session_table(D, *k, invert=True, height_ref="prominence") for k in sw.READINGS}
RAWP = {k: sw.session_table(D, *k, invert=False, height_ref="prominence") for k in sw.READINGS}
THP = {k: sw.thresholds(TABP[k]) for k in sw.READINGS}
TAB, RAW, TH = TABW[1.0], RAWW[1.0], THW[1.0]

                        for k in sw.READINGS])
print(summary.to_string(index=False))

# Null test of the detector: detections before the onset and after the stimulus, where no AP is
# expected, against those during the stimulus, per 100 ms of recording, both height readings.
def null_table(TABS):
    rows = []
    for href, T in TABS.items():
        for k in sw.READINGS:
            t = T[k]
            rows.append(dict(reading=rname(k), height_as=href,
                             during=int(t.n_aps.sum()), during_per_100ms=100 * t.n_aps.sum() / t.stim_ms.sum(),
                             before=int(t.null_pre.sum()), before_per_100ms=100 * t.null_pre.sum() / (sw.ONSET_MS * len(t)),
                             after=int(t.null_post.sum()), after_per_100ms=100 * t.null_post.sum() / t.post_ms.sum(),
                             sessions_with_after=int((t.null_post > 0).sum())))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

NULL = null_table({"value": TAB, "prominence": TABP})
print(f"window after the stimulus: {TAB[sw.READINGS[0]].post_ms.min():.0f} to {TAB[sw.READINGS[0]].post_ms.max():.0f} ms per session")
print(NULL.round(2).to_string(index=False))
nv = NULL[NULL.height_as == "value"].set_index("reading")
npm = NULL[NULL.height_as == "prominence"].set_index("reading")
print("\nafter-stimulus rate over during-stimulus rate, whole frame, height (b): value",
      round(nv.loc["whole/a/b"].after_per_100ms / nv.loc["whole/a/b"].during_per_100ms, 2),
      "| prominence", round(npm.loc["whole/a/b"].after_per_100ms / npm.loc["whole/a/b"].during_per_100ms, 2))

The detections after the stimulus, where no AP is expected, are the detector's false positives under each reading. Under the whole frame with height (b), the value reading makes 46 detections after the stimulus, in 23 of the 65 sessions: 0.91 per 100 ms, against 2.09 per 100 ms during the stimulus. With the height as prominence it makes 1 (0.02 per 100 ms, against 1.43 during). The Otsu-ROI readings make false detections either way (after the stimulus 0.37 to 0.53 per 100 ms with the value and the 5% height, 0.24 to 1.28 with prominence). So for the claims that count APs on the inverted trace, this record adopts the whole frame, height (b) and the height as prominence, an assumption made after verification round 1; the value reading, the claims file's first, is shown beside it in every section.

figs1-eight-neurons¶

The Di-8-ANEPPS control experiments were made on eight neurons, at field strengths tested in a random sequence.

Criterion: neurons counted from the dataset's subjects, sessions or cell identifiers, each recording once; expected 8, tolerance 0. The order of fields is reported, not judged.

figs1-aps-as-emission-decrease¶

With Di-8-ANEPPS, APs appear as brief reductions of emission, opposite in sign to FluoVolt.

Criterion: per neuron, over its sessions at fields above its threshold (F4), AP detection (O3) on the trace as recorded and on the inverted trace; reproduced when in every neuron with APs the inverted trace yields more APs than the trace as recorded in more than 75% of its sessions with APs.

In [10]:
def emission(TAB, RAW, TH):
    rows = []
    for k in sw.READINGS:
        inv, raw, th = TAB[k], RAW[k], dict(zip(TH[k].subject, TH[k].threshold))
        ok_all, n_neur = True, 0
        for s in sorted(inv.subject.unique()):
            sel = (inv.subject == s) & (inv.field > th[s])
            ni, nr = inv.n_aps[sel].values, raw.n_aps[sel].values
            has = (ni > 0) | (nr > 0)
            if has.sum() == 0:
                continue
            n_neur += 1
            frac = float(np.mean(ni[has] > nr[has]))
            ok_all &= frac > 0.75
            rows.append(dict(reading=rname(k), subject=s, sessions_above_thr=int(sel.sum()), sessions_with_aps=int(has.sum()),
                             aps_inverted=int(ni.sum()), aps_as_recorded=int(nr.sum()), frac_more_inverted=round(frac, 2)))
        rows.append(dict(reading=rname(k), subject="ALL", sessions_with_aps=n_neur, frac_more_inverted=None, ok=ok_all))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

figs1-near-threshold-delayed-aps¶

Near threshold, 2-kHz sine waves elicited one or a few delayed APs in Di-8-ANEPPS neurons.

Criterion: per neuron, its near-threshold sessions (O4 (a) at the threshold field, (b) fields up to 10% above it); the median session has 1 to 3 APs and its first AP is delayed (O5 (a) at least 100 ms after onset, (b) later than the median first-AP latency of the neuron's sessions at higher fields). Reproduced when this holds in more than half of the neurons with APs.

def near_threshold(tab, th, o4):
    out = []
    for s in sorted(tab.subject.unique()):
        g = tab[tab.subject == s]
        t0 = th[s]
        if np.isnan(t0):
            continue
        near = g[g.field == t0] if o4 == "a" else g[(g.field >= t0) & (g.field <= 1.1 * t0)]
        higher = g[(g.field > near.field.max()) & (g.n_aps > 0)]
        out.append(dict(subject=s, threshold=t0, near_sessions=len(near), median_aps=float(np.median(near.n_aps)),
                        aps=near.n_aps.tolist(), median_first_ms=float(np.nanmedian(near.first_ms)),
                        higher_median_first_ms=float(np.nanmedian(higher.first_ms)) if len(higher) else np.nan))
    return pd.DataFrame(out)

def near_all(TAB, TH):
    rows, detail = [], {}
    for k in sw.READINGS:
        th = dict(zip(TH[k].subject, TH[k].threshold))
        for o4 in "ab":
            nt = near_threshold(TAB[k], th, o4)
            detail[(k, o4)] = nt
            few = (nt.median_aps >= 1) & (nt.median_aps <= 3)
            for o5 in "ab":
                delayed = nt.median_first_ms >= 100 if o5 == "a" else nt.median_first_ms > nt.higher_median_first_ms
                n_ok = int((few & delayed).sum())
                rows.append(dict(reading=rname(k), O4=o4, O5=o5, neurons_with_aps=len(nt), neurons_meeting=n_ok,
                                 reproduced=n_ok > len(nt) / 2))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows), detail

Result: not reproduced, resting on an assumption (changed from partially reproduced after verification round 3, see the end of this cell). Under the adopted readings (whole frame, F0 (a), height (b) as prominence, O5 (a), a first AP at least 100 ms after onset), every neuron fires a median of 1 AP at its threshold field, but the first AP comes at a median 137 ms in subject 4 only, and at 63 ms (subject 3) and 6 ms (subject 2) in the others, so 1 of 3 neurons meets the criterion. Each neuron's near-threshold AP is later than its APs at higher fields (2.7, 8.3 and 21.8 ms). With the height as prominence the criterion is met in 20 of 48 reading combinations: 0 of 24 under O5 (a) and 20 of 24 under O5 (b), the delay relative to the neuron's higher fields. With the height as the value it is met in 19 of 48 (6 of 24 under O5 (a), 13 of 24 under O5 (b)); under whole/a/b, subject 2 then fires 2 APs at threshold with the first at 108 ms and subject 4 one at 201 ms, so 2 of 3 neurons meet it, but that reading also detects APs after the stimulus (null test). So near threshold one or a few APs hold in all three neurons, later than at higher fields, and a delay of 100 ms or more in one to two of the three, depending on the height reading.

Why not reproduced: the criterion is one test per neuron, which needs the median near-threshold session to have 1 to 3 APs and its first AP to be delayed, and it is met when more than half of the neurons pass that test. Under the adopted readings (whole/a/b, height as prominence, O5 (a)) 1 of 3 neurons passes, under O4 (a) and (b) alike, and the criterion is met in 0 of 24 combinations under O5 (a) with prominence (6 of 24 with the value). "Partially" described the two halves of the per-neuron test, which the criterion does not judge apart. Under O5 (b), "delayed" relative to the neuron's own higher fields, every neuron would pass, so the outcome rests on the reading of "delayed".

figs1-stronger-field-shorter-delay-sustained-firing¶

In Di-8-ANEPPS neurons, increasing the field strength reduced the delay to the first AP and induced sustained firing.

Criterion: per neuron with sessions with APs at 3 or more fields, the Spearman correlation of first-AP latency with field; reproduced when negative in more than half of those neurons and more than half of all neurons show sustained firing (O6) in some session. F5 rates are reported.

def stronger(TAB):
    rows = []
    for k in sw.READINGS:
        tab = TAB[k]
        rhos, sf = [], []
        for s in sorted(tab.subject.unique()):
            g = tab[tab.subject == s]
            ga = g[g.n_aps > 0]
            rho = stats.spearmanr(ga.field, ga.first_ms) if ga.field.nunique() >= 3 else None
            if rho is not None:
                rhos.append(rho.statistic)
            sf.append(bool(g.sust_firing.any()))
            rows.append(dict(reading=rname(k), subject=s, fields_with_aps=int(ga.field.nunique()),
                             rho=None if rho is None else round(rho.statistic, 2),
                             p=None if rho is None else round(rho.pvalue, 3), sustained_firing=sf[-1],
                             max_rate_hz=round(np.nanmax(g.rate_hz), 1) if g.rate_hz.notna().any() else None))
        neg = np.sum(np.array(rhos) < 0)
        rows.append(dict(reading=rname(k), subject="ALL", fields_with_aps=len(rhos), rho=int(neg), sustained_firing=int(sum(sf)),
                         max_rate_hz=None, reproduced=(len(rhos) > 0 and neg > len(rhos) / 2) and sum(sf) > len(sf) / 2))
    c4 = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    allc4 = c4[c4.subject == "ALL"][["reading", "fields_with_aps", "rho", "sustained_firing", "reproduced"]]
    allc4.columns = ["reading", "neurons_3plus_fields", "negative_rho", "neurons_sustained_firing", "reproduced"]
    return c4[c4.subject != "ALL"], allc4

Result: reproduced, resting on an assumption. Under the adopted readings (whole frame, height (b) as prominence) the latency correlates negatively with field in all 3 neurons (Spearman rho -0.63, -0.03 and -0.50; p 0.007, 0.88 and 0.058) and all 3 show sustained firing (5, 11 and 10 sessions). With the height as prominence the criterion is met under 10 of 12 readings and all 6 with height (b); with the height as the value, also 10 of 12 and 6 of 6, with more sessions of sustained firing (8, 22 and 11 under whole/a/b), part of which the null test shows to be noise on a raised baseline. Most single correlations are not significant (rho from -0.94 to 0.50 over readings). It fails under the 5% height with the whole frame, where few Di-8-ANEPPS APs reach 5%. The earlier 2-ms bound gives the same 10 of 12 readings.

figs1-culminates-in-sustained-depolarization¶

In Di-8-ANEPPS neurons, the strongest fields replaced firing with sustained depolarization (excitation followed by inhibition of firing).

Criterion: per neuron, its sessions at its highest field; reproduced when more than half of the neurons show sustained depolarization (O6) at their highest field and sustained firing or more APs at some lower field. O6 levels (a) 5 SD of the trace before onset, (b) half the neuron's median AP height. A neuron counts when most of its highest-field sessions show it (a standard choice).

In [13]:
def bleach_corrected(tab):
    """Late mean minus the mean late dF of the neuron's sessions with no AP (variant, after round 1)."""
    tab = tab.copy()
    base = tab[tab.n_aps == 0].groupby("subject").late_mean.mean()
    tab["late_base"] = tab.subject.map(base).fillna(0.0)
    late = tab.late_mean - tab.late_base
    tab["sust_depol_a"] = (tab.late_aps == 0) & (late > 5 * tab.pre_sd)
    tab["sust_depol_b"] = (tab.late_aps == 0) & (late > tab.level_b)
    return tab

def culminates(TAB, bleach=False):
    rows = []
    for k in sw.READINGS:
        tab = bleach_corrected(TAB[k]) if bleach else TAB[k]
        for lev in "ab":
            n_ok, per = 0, []
            for s in sorted(tab.subject.unique()):
                g = tab[tab.subject == s]
                top, low = g[g.field == g.field.max()], g[g.field < g.field.max()]
                sd = top[f"sust_depol_{lev}"].mean() > 0.5
                more = bool(low.sust_firing.any() or (low.n_aps.max() > top.n_aps.max()))
                n_ok += sd and more
                per.append(f"{s[:1]}:{'D' if sd else '-'}{'F' if more else '-'}")
            rows.append(dict(reading=rname(k), level=lev, neurons=" ".join(per), meeting=n_ok, reproduced=n_ok > 1.5))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

Result: not reproduced. At most 1 of the 3 neurons meets the criterion under any of the 24 reading and level combinations, where more than half are needed, with the height as the value or as prominence, and with either width bound. Subjects 2 and 4 were not stimulated above 234 V/cm, close to their thresholds, and never reach sustained depolarization. Subject 3, stimulated up to 504 V/cm, meets it only with the whole frame and the 5% height (and with prominence also under the Otsu ROI with level (b)); with the whole frame and height (b) its late inverted dF is 2.9 to 3.3% at 396 to 504 V/cm, against 1.4 to 2.4% at most lower fields, and it keeps 1 AP in the last 100 ms at 504 V/cm with the height as prominence (6 with the value). The inverted trace drifts up from bleaching: the late mean of the AP-free sessions is 1.36 to 1.57%. Subtracting each neuron's AP-free late mean from its late dF, no neuron meets the criterion under any combination.

FluoVolt reference group (outside this dataset)¶

The with_inputs claims compare these neurons with FluoVolt neurons stimulated by 250-ms unmodulated 2-kHz sine waves in NaCl solution (claims file: DANDI:001030 and 001032 to 001035, assigned from their titles). 001030 holds only 2-s ramped waves in sodium gluconate, so none of its sessions fit. 001034 is checked against 001032 first.

figs1-noisier-than-fluovolt¶

Di-8-ANEPPS traces were noisier than FluoVolt traces, as the dye has a lower voltage sensitivity.

Criterion: per neuron, the signal to noise ratio is the median AP height over the SD of dF before the onset; readings of "noisier" (a) that ratio, (b) the SD itself. Reproduced when the Di-8-ANEPPS median is worse than the FluoVolt median under both. A two-sided unpaired t test (F6) is reported, and the median Di-8-ANEPPS AP height beside the FluoVolt 11.3% (Methods).

In [15]:
FTABW = {w: {k: sw.session_table(FV, *k, invert=False, min_width_ms=w) for k in sw.READINGS} for w in (1.0, 2.0)}
FTAB = FTABW[1.0]
FTABP = {k: sw.session_table(FV, *k, invert=False, height_ref="prominence") for k in sw.READINGS}

def per_neuron_noise(tab):
    g = tab.explode("ap_heights")
    med_h = g.groupby("subject").ap_heights.apply(lambda s: float(np.nanmedian(s.astype(float))) if s.notna().any() else np.nan)
    sd = tab.groupby("subject").pre_sd.median()
    return pd.DataFrame({"median_ap_height": med_h, "pre_sd": sd, "snr": med_h / sd})

def noise(TAB, FTAB):
    rows = []
    for k in sw.READINGS:
        di, fv = per_neuron_noise(TAB[k]), per_neuron_noise(FTAB[k])
        snr_t = stats.ttest_ind(di.snr.dropna(), fv.snr.dropna())
        sd_t = stats.ttest_ind(di.pre_sd, fv.pre_sd)
        rows.append(dict(reading=rname(k), di8_snr=di.snr.median(), fv_snr=fv.snr.median(), p_snr=snr_t.pvalue,
                         di8_sd=di.pre_sd.median(), fv_sd=fv.pre_sd.median(), p_sd=sd_t.pvalue,
                         di8_height=di.median_ap_height.median(), fv_height=fv.median_ap_height.median(),
                         n_di8=int(di.snr.notna().sum()), n_fv=int(fv.snr.notna().sum()),
                         worse_both=(di.snr.median() < fv.snr.median()) and (di.pre_sd.median() > fv.pre_sd.median())))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

c6 = noise(TAB, FTAB)
print(c6.round(3).to_string(index=False))
print(f"Di-8-ANEPPS worse under both measures in {int(c6.worse_both.sum())} of {len(c6)} readings")
c6w = noise(TABW[2.0], FTABW[2.0])
print(f"earlier 2-ms bound: worse under both in {int(c6w.worse_both.sum())} of 12; SNR lower in {int((c6w.di8_snr < c6w.fv_snr).sum())}, "

Result: not reproduced. The criterion requires both measures and is met under none of the 12 readings, with either width bound or height reading. By the signal to noise ratio (a) the Di-8-ANEPPS median is lower than FluoVolt's under 10 of 12 readings with the height as the value (6 of 12 as prominence; whole frame 7.0 to 9.7 against 12.7 to 12.9, t test p from 0.001 to 0.14), because its median AP height is about half (3.7 to 6.7% against 10.1 to 14.5%; the FluoVolt value is near the paper's typical 11.3%). By the SD before the onset (b), the direct measure of noise, the Di-8-ANEPPS traces are less noisy (0.55 against 0.88% with the whole frame, p < 0.001; 1.24 against 1.57 or 3.05% with the Otsu ROI). The lower signal to noise ratio comes from the smaller APs the paper attributes to the dye's lower sensitivity, not from noisier traces.

figs1-effects-same-as-fluovolt¶

Overall, the effects of 2-kHz sine waves in Di-8-ANEPPS neurons did not differ from those with FluoVolt, so the excitation by unmodulated sine waves is not a sensitization by FluoVolt.

Criterion: the response pattern holds when figs1-near-threshold-delayed-aps, figs1-stronger-field-shorter-delay-sustained-firing and figs1-culminates-in-sustained-depolarization are reproduced; the 1-AP thresholds (F4) of the Di-8-ANEPPS neurons are compared with those of the FluoVolt neurons by a two-sided unpaired t test at p < 0.05. Reproduced when the pattern holds and the test finds no difference.

The files state amplitudes differently: 001032 to 001035 give "peak-to-peak" volts, 001272 "amplitude" in volts, 001030 "one polarity; peak-to-peak would be two-fold larger", all with 36 V/cm per volt. Two readings are run: (i) the volts as stated, times 36, in both groups; (ii) the FluoVolt volts halved (if 001272 states one polarity). DANDI:001271, FluoVolt recorded in 2024 with the same description wording as 001272, gives a check of which scale 001272's "amplitude" is on.

def same_thr(TH, FTAB):
    rows = []
    for k in sw.READINGS:
        di = TH[k].dropna(subset=["threshold"])
        fv = sw.thresholds(FTAB[k]).dropna(subset=["threshold"])
        for unit, fvf in (("i", fv.threshold.values), ("ii", fv.threshold.values / 2)):
            tt = stats.ttest_ind(di.threshold.values, fvf)
            d = di.threshold.mean() - fvf.mean()
            sp = np.sqrt(((len(di) - 1) * di.threshold.var() + (len(fvf) - 1) * fvf.var()) / (len(di) + len(fvf) - 2))
            se = sp * np.sqrt(1 / len(di) + 1 / len(fvf))
            tc = stats.t.ppf(0.975, len(di) + len(fvf) - 2)
            rows.append(dict(reading=rname(k), unit=unit, n_di8=len(di), di8_mean=di.threshold.mean(),
                             n_fv=len(fvf), fv_mean=fvf.mean(), diff=d, ci_lo=d - tc * se, ci_hi=d + tc * se,
                             p=tt.pvalue, one_sample_vs_57_7_p=stats.ttest_1samp(di.threshold, 57.7).pvalue,
                             differ=tt.pvalue < 0.05))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

c7 = same_thr(TH, FTAB)
print(c7.round(3).to_string(index=False))
for u in ("i", "ii"):
    s = c7[c7.unit == u]
    print(f"unit reading ({u}): difference at p < 0.05 in {int(s.differ.sum())} of {len(s)} readings")
c7p = same_thr(THP, FTABP)
for u in ("i", "ii"):

Result: partially reproduced, resting on an assumption. Under unit reading (i), the volts as the files state them, which this record adopts, the t test finds no difference between the Di-8-ANEPPS (n = 2 or 3, mean 108 to 152 V/cm) and FluoVolt (n = 20 to 27, mean 140 to 178 V/cm) 1-AP thresholds under all 12 readings (p from 0.27 to 0.98; difference -43 to 1 V/cm, 95% intervals as wide as -156 to 124 V/cm), nor with the height as prominence (p from 0.15 to 0.64). The 001271 check gives no evidence against (i): its FluoVolt thresholds in the 2024 "amplitude" volts (mean 3.70 V) and those of 001032 to 001035 in "peak-to-peak" volts (4.20 V) do not differ (p = 0.29), which does not show that the scales are equal. Under reading (ii) the Di-8-ANEPPS thresholds are higher in 9 of 12 readings (p from 0.002 to 0.017; 8 of 12 as prominence). The response pattern holds only in part: the stronger-field claim is reproduced, the near-threshold and sustained-depolarization claims are not, so the criterion's condition for reproduced is not met, while its condition for not reproduced (a threshold difference) is not met under the adopted reading either. The FluoVolt mean under (i), about 150 V/cm, is far above the paper's 57.7 V/cm.

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's: the soma outline is not deposited, so three ROI readings are run; AP detection, delay, sustained firing and sustained depolarization follow the claims file's readings, since the paper describes Figure S1 in words only, with the AP width bound of 1 to 20 ms the claims file now gives (the earlier 2 to 20 ms is shown beside it). Where readings disagree this record adopts, for Di-8-ANEPPS, the whole frame, the AP height reading (b), 5 SD of the trace before onset (the paper says this dye is less sensitive than FluoVolt and its 5% level was set for FluoVolt), and the height measured as prominence, since with the height as the dF value the detector finds nearly half as many peaks after the stimulus as during it on the bleaching-raised inverted trace.

What was found about the dataset: it holds 3 neurons, where the paper reports 8; the frames are 16 x 16 pixels, where the Methods give 64 x 64; the stimulus onset is not stored; the amplitude is given in volts without saying whether it is peak or peak-to-peak, and the files of the paper's deposits apply the same 36 V/cm per volt to peak-to-peak and one-polarity values; every file's description says the experiment was a vehicle control for tetrodotoxin, which this experiment was not; the first frame of every file is an artefact; several sessions are under 20 s apart, where the Methods give 20 to 60 s; the 80 2-kHz unmodulated files of DANDI:001034 have frame stacks identical to those of DANDI:001032 (its other files are not compared here).
